# Taksim

Taksim is an Intelligence Control Plane for coding agents.

Canonical site: https://taksim.edgee.tech
Documentation: https://taksim.edgee.tech/docs
Getting started: https://taksim.edgee.tech/docs/getting-started
Sign-in (optional): https://taksim.edgee.tech/docs/sign-in
Pricing: https://taksim.edgee.tech/pricing
Privacy: https://taksim.edgee.tech/privacy

Current client boundary (verified 2026-09-26):
- Claude Code: managed sessions and historical import.
- Codex: managed observation and historical import; native model selection in v0.
- Devin: managed sessions and historical import.
- GitHub Copilot Coding Agent: historical visibility only; no managed launch.

History import only, no managed launch and no routing (`taksim history import --client <name>`). Not in the v0.1.1 release: available when you build Taksim from main, and in the next release.
- AgentBoard (`agentboard`): history import only; no managed launch, no routing.
- Agent Workstation (`agentworkstation`): history import only; no managed launch, no routing.
- Devin Desktop (`devin_desktop`, formerly Windsurf): history import and judge backlog only; a subscription product Taksim never launches or routes.
- Kilo Code (`kilo`): history import and judging only; managed launch and routing are deferred.
- OpenCode (`opencode`): history import and judging only; managed launch and routing are deferred.
- Pi / Oh My Pi (`pi`): history import and judging only; no managed launch or routing.

Taksim governs policy, quality, privacy, budget, eligibility, evidence, direct resource selection, and approved provider-native delegation. It is not positioned as a proprietary request-level multi-model router.

Sign-in is optional and off by default: install Taksim and run `taksim claude` or `taksim codex` with no account. Hosted sign-in only activates when an operator sets `Identity__Enabled=true`, in which case it supports Google/GitHub browser sign-in and explicit Solo terms, and stores device credentials in Windows Credential Manager (up to 24 hours, no automatic refresh). The public installer remains v0.1.1, which predates this opt-in sign-in flow; it currently requires a source/development build.

Everything runs locally on 127.0.0.1 by default; nothing leaves the machine unless you opt in to a hosted Taksim feature. There is no default hosted routing-advice service. This does not describe the native AI client itself: Claude Code, Codex, and similar clients still send prompts and responses to their own provider under that provider's terms, independent of Taksim.

Subscription traffic is observed, not rewritten: when Claude Code runs on a Claude subscription (Max/Pro, `Authorization: Bearer`), Taksim records what it would have chosen and reports cost/quota comparisons via `taksim report baseline`, without rewriting the model. Model rewrite applies only to API-key traffic (`x-api-key`); power users can opt out of the observe-only default with `TAKSIM_ALLOW_SUBSCRIPTION_REWRITE=1` at their own risk.
